page: Microsoft Azure EC64ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is driven by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor using the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via two threads per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 512.0 GB, establishing an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Local ephemeral storage is provisioned via 2,577 GB of integrated SSD media, and the server supports Azure Premium Storage. The configuration does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. On the instruction set level, the processor features standard AVX, SHA-NI, AES, and VAES extensions for hardware-accelerated encryption and hashing, though it lacks support for AVX-512 and AMX extensions.

Benchmark evaluation shows robust parallel compute efficiency, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 74,103.18, which falls into the top 25 percent of tested machines. Single-core processing reaches 2,118.86 under stress-ng, placing in the median 50 percent tier. Memory and transaction subsystem benchmarks demonstrate 62.26 million Redis SET operations per second, also ranking within the top 25 percent bracket.

The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with fast local solid-state storage offers balanced density for data-heavy applications requiring fast access to state. The lack of AVX-512 and hardware GPUs limits utility for specialized machine learning training or advanced vector-heavy calculations. Workload fit includes in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, analytics platforms, and relational database servers.
